title: Beyond UCSV? Macro-Financial Signals in the U.S. Inflation Forecast Frontier

detail.title: Beyond UCSV? Macro-Financial Signals in the U.S. Inflation Forecast Frontier
detail.abstract: We ask whether macro-financial signals carry forecast information beyond the Stock-Watson (2007) UCSV benchmark for U.S. inflation, and we report a calibrated answer. On a strictly anti-lookahead causal panel of CPI, core CPI, PCE and core PCE at horizons of 3 to 24 months, with HAC-based Clark-West and Diebold-Mariano-Harvey-Leybourne-Newbold inference, signal-based specifications deliver large point gains over UCSV and remain significant under raw and Benjamini-Hochberg control. Under the more conservative Romano-Wolf stepdown, on the broad family or on a transparent primary-model family, no individual signal specification beats UCSV in a family-wise sense, a property the signal literature largely shares. The Hansen, Lunde and Nason (2011) Model Confidence Set then sharpens the question. In the 25 country-target-horizon cells where the MCS is computable, UCSV is excluded from the 90% MCS in 19 cells while signal-based models remain inside in 20. The result concentrates in ten informative U.S. cells, core CPI at horizons 6, 12, 18 and 24; headline CPI at horizons 12, 18 and 24; and headline PCE at horizons 12, 18 and 24, where the MCS is tight (at most six surviving models), a signal specification is inside the 90% set, and UCSV is outside with MCS p-values between 0.006 and 0.064. The supportable headline is therefore narrower than "predictors beat the benchmark" and stronger than "predictors and benchmark are equivalent": in informative U.S. cells, macro-financial signal content lies within the frontier of best forecasts and discriminates against the field's standard benchmark, even when no single specification wins individually under the strictest family-wise control. The result survives under real-time vintage data from ALFRED for the six implemented U.S. series: nine of the ten core cells are preserved, with the failure occurring only at the shortest-horizon core CPI cell where data revisions are most consequential. Brazilian results, reported as complementary evidence, are directionally consistent for the IGP-M and the IPCA aggregates but rest on wider MCS sets and are less informative on power grounds.

title: The κ-Standard: Debt-Free Money Creation under a Riba-Free Convergence Intensity (Uniting the Chicago Plan and Islamic Full-Reserve Monetary Theory)

detail.title: The κ-Standard: Debt-Free Money Creation under a Riba-Free Convergence Intensity (Uniting the Chicago Plan and Islamic Full-Reserve Monetary Theory)
detail.abstract:
Two traditions of monetary reform, the Islamic interest-free programme of Al-Jarhi (1981) and Chapra (1985), and the Western full-reserve tradition of Fisher (1936) and Benes & Kumhof (2012), independently reached the same design: money should be created debt-free by the state and separated from interest-bearing bank credit. Both stalled at the same point. Once money creation is divorced from interest-bearing debt, the assets that back the money base must still be priced, and the natural pricing object, the risk-free interest rate r, is precisely the riba the reform sets out to remove. Neither tradition supplied a riba-free price at which the market could clear. This paper provides one.

Building on the convergence intensity κ of Ackerer et al. (2025), shown by the companion papers to be a riba-free, no-arbitrage pricing primitive estimable from real sukuk markets, we construct the κ-Standard: a monetary architecture in which (i) base money equals the κ-priced value of a portfolio of sovereign perpetual sukuk, so that money is sovereign equity rather than debt; (ii) new money is created only by monetising new real-sector projects at their κ-implied price, tethering money growth to real output; (iii) open-market operations transmit through the system-wide convergence intensity κ̄ rather than an interest rate, with the central bank setting the quantity of money while the market sets the price of capital; and (iv) commercial banks operate under one hundred per cent reserves, splitting into fee-based (ujrah) custody and profit-sharing (mudarabah) investment.

We derive the law of motion of the money supply and show that a shock to κ̄ (a system-wide credit deterioration) contracts the base automatically. We then derive a countercyclical issuance rule that neutralises this revaluation channel and holds the base on a target growth path. The correction is bounded by available real capacity and a Sovereign Stabilisation Fund, a deliberate trade of unbounded-but-unbacked fiat stabilisation for bounded-but-backed stabilisation (roughly $3.6 bn per 100 bp for the full real sukuk universe).

We are explicit about what the architecture does not achieve: it removes debt-financed and unbacked money creation and ties money to real-asset value, but its price level is determinate only under a fiscal closure (the sole determinacy regime an interest-free system admits, since it has no interest-rate instrument), and a companion paper shows this survives in full general equilibrium. Its stabilisation is bounded. We propose κ as a candidate riba-free clearing object that lets a full-reserve money base clear without an interest rate, serving both the Chicago-Plan and Islamic full-reserve programmes; we do not claim it was the sole obstacle to either programme's adoption, which is substantially institutional and political. The empirical reality of κ rests so far only on the authors' own companion working papers, pending independent replication, so we present this as a theoretical architecture.

title: Subjects and Objects of God: Non-state Normative Orders and International Corporate Theology

detail.title: Subjects and Objects of God: Non-state Normative Orders and International Corporate Theology
detail.abstract: Normative orders, whether divine, state, or corporate, allocate standing not by personhood but by address. A subject is an entity whose interior states the sovereign cares about and speaks to; an object is an entity the order governs purely instrumentally, as a means of changing what subjects think. This Article reconstructs that grammar from the canonical text in which it is most fully elaborated: the Hebrew Bible, whose narrative assigns subjecthood to man, to Satan, and to kingdoms, while deploying weather, plague, family, and conquered populations as instruments of divine pedagogy. The Article then argues that the subject/object boundary is not an ontological datum but what Karen Barad calls an "agential cut," enacted by the order's own apparatus of address, and that the biblical text both constructs this cut and repeatedly subverts it. Finally, the Article argues that the same grammar, and the same instability, appear in the internal legal orders of multinational corporations, whose compliance regimes address employees as subjects while governing supply chains as objects, and whose boundaries are being recut in real time by whistleblower statutes, worker-reclassification litigation, and human-rights due-diligence legislation. Standing, the Article concludes, is best understood as a theory of address.

title: The Organization Was Warned: Labor Compliance, Coso, and the Governance of Known Employment Risk

detail.title: The Organization Was Warned: Labor Compliance, Coso, and the Governance of Known Employment Risk
detail.abstract: This article examines labor compliance through the lens of risk management, internal controls, and responsible decision-making. It argues that the maturity of labor compliance programs should not be measured merely by the existence of policies, training sessions, reporting channels, working-time controls, occupational health and safety procedures, or risk matrices. The central issue lies in what organizations do after employment-related risks become known. In many cases, labor risk does not arise suddenly. It is preceded by excessive working hours, repeated complaints, health-related absences, turnover, safety incidents, harassment allegations, weak third-party oversight, data protection failures, or recurring litigation patterns. Drawing on COSO, ISO 31000, internal control theory, behavioral insights, and the Brazilian legal framework as a jurisdictional case study, the article proposes the concept of conscious employment liability: liability arising not merely from the objective breach of labor standards, but from the persistence of risky labor practices after sufficient warning signs, indicators, complaints, or internal alerts. The article concludes that effective labor compliance should be understood as an institutional engineering of responsible decision-making. Its function is not to assume that human nature will become virtuous by decree, but to design structures that transform known labor risk into traceability, escalation, mitigation, accountability, and organizational learning. The decisive question is no longer whether the organization had a compliance program. It is whether the organization, once warned, was institutionally capable of deciding differently.

detail.title: Quotas and Reserves in Job Matching
detail.abstract: Regulations imposing hiring constraints are widely used to promote diversity in labor markets. Motivated by these interventions, this paper studies their effects on the welfare of minority workers in stable allocations. Building on a Crawford--Knoer framework, we show that such regulations can unintentionally reduce minority welfare. Using firm-optimal and worker-optimal stable allocations as benchmarks, we characterize the class of policies that, across all markets, never reduce minority welfare under either allocation. This class consists only of the null policy and policies that exclude non-minority workers from the market without imposing reserves. We then introduce policy rules, which allow policies to depend on the assignment observed prior to intervention. Restricting attention to environments with two worker groups, we characterize the set of policy rules that never reduce the welfare of minority workers.

title: Bqmm: Bayesian Multilevel Quantile Regression in R

detail.title: Bqmm: Bayesian Multilevel Quantile Regression in R
detail.abstract: Quantile regression describes how covariates shift the conditional quantiles of an outcome, not merely its mean, and is indispensable when effects are heterogeneous across the response distribution. When data are clustered or longitudinal, a mixed-effects formulation is needed. I present bqmm, an R package for Bayesian multilevel quantile regression built on the asymmetric Laplace working likelihood and Stan. The package offers an lme4-style formula interface with nested and crossed random effects, optional LKJ-correlated random effects, estimation of one or several quantiles in a single call, post-hoc non-crossing rearrangement, and a transparent menu of fixed-effect interval methods-the naive posterior, the Yang-Wang-He (2016) sandwich correction, and the infinitesimal jackknife-because the asymmetric Laplace likelihood is misspecified and naive credible intervals can be invalid. The paper describes the model and software design, illustrates usage on longitudinal growth data, summarises a validation study (parameter recovery, simulation-based calibration, and a coverage study), and compares bqmm with related software.

detail.abstract: Electronic Value Added Tax (E-VAT) schemes play an important role in the process of tax administration modernization in South Asia but have vastly varying revenue effects in countries that have broadly similar tax policy goals. This study aims to discuss the maturity of E-VAT system, the performance of VAT/GST revenue in six selected South Asian economies (S.A.E.) with specific reference to Bangladesh, the behavior of taxpayers and challenges in implementing E-VAT system in those selected S.A.E. It follows a sequential explanatory mixed methods design, which involves secondary country-year data for fiscal years 2019-2024 and 25 semi-structured interviews with 5 NBR officials, 10 VAT consultants and 10 VAT-registered SME taxpayers. Due to the small panel sample (n = 25), this exploratory OLS regression analysis is not meant to uncover exact causal relationships. Although the rate of the standard VAT rate in Bangladesh is 15%, and the E-VAT platform has been operational since 2019, Bangladesh has a low VAT-to-GDP ratio of about 3.6%, compared to Nepal (5.3%) and India (6-7%) and the Maldives (approximately 12%). Additionally, as shown in interview evidence, there are ongoing institutional and operational challenges that limit the actual use of the einvoice tool, such as: Segregated revenue databases; Unreliability of the portal during peaks of einvoice filing; Low levels of taxpayer training; Poor taxpayer grievance mechanisms; and the lack of mandation for e-invoicing. The study suggests the Bangladesh E-VAT Adoption Framework (BEVAF) that correlates institutional enablers, technology platform maturity and behavioral compliance outcomes from an institutional perspective. The results confirm a staged reform program focusing on the following areas: e-invoicing, integration of databases, taxpayer assistance, audit risk scoring, accessing invoices on mobile devices, and reform of penalty procedures.

detail.abstract: This paper develops an integrative analytical framework within institutional and evolutionary economics. Drawing on a dialectical synthesis of Hegel's emphasis on external reality as the driver of consciousness and Marx's historical materialism, the study introduces two conceptual innovations: the notion of "shells" as a multi-level ontological unit and the Principle of Uncertainty as a normative mechanism for managing persistent misalignment between external challenges and internal structures.The framework is applied to a comparative-historical analysis of post-reform trajectories in Russia, China, and India. Using standard indicators of annual GDP growth, total factor productivity (TFP), and the Worldwide Governance Indicators, the paper shows how the factor of uncertainty-arising from the imperfect reflection of rapidly changing external reality by collective consciousness-helps explain divergent long-term development paths. China's gradual multi-level approach minimized misalignment and maintained high adherence to the Principle of Uncertainty, producing sustained growth and institutional adaptation. India exhibited moderate and spatially heterogeneous misalignment due to federal experimentation. Russia's rapid dismantling of central shells generated significantly higher misalignment and lower adherence to the Principle of Uncertainty, resulting in greater volatility.The study demonstrates that the quality of alignment across hierarchical shells and the degree of adherence to the Principle of Uncertainty are critical determinants of sustained economic performance. It also offers concrete policy implications for managing contemporary challenges such as artificial intelligence and ecological constraints.

title: Designated for Success? Testing for Cherry-Picking in New York City's Opportunity Zone Designations Using Permutation Inference and Detrended Difference-in-Differences

detail.title: Designated for Success? Testing for Cherry-Picking in New York City's Opportunity Zone Designations Using Permutation Inference and Detrended Difference-in-Differences
detail.abstract:
The Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 established the Opportunity Zone (OZ) program, a federal initiative meant to encourage private investment in economically distressed census tracts. Officials select designated tracts from an eligible pool at their discretion. This study examines whether New York City's 306 Opportunity Zone census tracts were cherry-picked—systematically selected based on pre-existing favorable trajectories rather than genuine economic distress. I test whether OZ designation caused meaningful demographic and economic shifts observed in designated tracts or whether those shifts merely reflect pre-existing trends. I conducted three analyses using American Community Survey five-year estimates for eight outcomes. First, a permutation test compared the pre-policy growth trends of OZ tracts against 1,000 randomly selected groups of eligible tracts, finding that OZ neighborhoods were already gaining White residents at an unusual rate before designation (p = 0.010). Second, a standard difference-in-differences (DiD) model with Monte Carlo permutation inference produced statistically significant shifts in racial composition and home values. Third, I removed each neighborhood's pre-existing growth trajectory before re-estimating the policy's effects in a detrended DiD. After detrending, every previously significant result—the increase in White population share, the decline in Hispanic population share, and the rise in median home value—fell outside statistical significance.

These results suggest that the changes attributed to Opportunity Zones were largely underway before the policy took effect. The discretionary selection process may have allowed officials to designate tracts already on favorable trajectories, creating the appearance of policy success even when the policy had no detectable effect. I recommend that future place-based investment programs adopt transparent, formula-driven selection criteria, publish tract-level scores, and require pre-trend audits before crediting observed improvements to the program.

detail.abstract:
The cross-border spillover effects of shifts in U.S. monetary policy have long been a focus of academics and policymakers alike. A common finding in the literature is that changes in the stance of U.S. monetary policy have sizable effects on economic activity and financial markets in emerging market economies (EMEs). In this post, we analyze one specific aspect of these spillovers: how EMEs fared through the U.S. monetary policy tightening cycle of 2022-23 relative to the predictions of a model, which was calibrated to capture empirically relevant features of these economies based on historical data. We find that more vulnerable EMEs fared better in both financial market and growth outcomes than would be expected from our model, while the relatively less vulnerable fared a bit better than the model predictions for financial outcomes but substantially worse for growth outcomes.

detail.abstract:
It seems fashionable these days to start by quoting Antonio Gramsci: “we in an interregnum – the old is dying, the new is yet to be born, we are surrounded by morbid symptoms”. The “old” is the international “rules-based” order that has prevailed since World War Two, or in the international trade regime, since the 1980s. Its breakdown is variously attributed to the rise of economic nationalism, great power rivalries, and populist politics that have enabled authoritarian government.

But too often those commentators forget that Gramsci was a communist imprisoned by Mussolini’s facist regime and chronicled the hegemonic crisis facing Italy’s ruling class and their system of governance in the 1920s. The morbid symptoms he observed – authoritarianism, political extremism, and social breakdown – were products of a political struggle over material and social relations, understood through the lens of historical materialism. Internationally, that was overlaid by the brutality and nihilism of colonisation and imperialism, which was beyond Gramsci’s immediate focus.

Translated to today, the same morbid symptoms of authoritarianism, political extremism and social breakdown need to be understood as products of hyper-globalised capitalism that has prevailed since the 1980s. And the deep disparities between rule-makers and rule-takers in the international trade and investment regime are built upon their colonial legacy, overlaid by new forms of militarisation and imperialism.

detail.abstract: The article is devoted to the development of a creative model for managing human capital and social responsibility of agricultural business, taking into account the tasks of food stability. The research focuses on the interaction of personnel parameters, technological development and production results, which is interpreted as a multidimensional system of dependencies. Methodologically, the work is based on a combination of the index approach, integral estimation and econometric modeling. A system of internal human capital indices is proposed, covering qualification, digital, motivational and analytical components, as well as the intensity of reskilling. The indicators are integrated into the generalized assessment index. The results showed that the impact of human capital and social responsibility on productivity is non-linear and enhanced by their interaction with technological parameters. It has been established that the main increase in production results is due to an interaction between the level of competencies and the digitalization of personnel work. It has been proven that human capital has an impact on food stability directly through the structure of production and the level of specialization. The practical significance of the study lies in the fact that the proposed toolkit predicts the results of the activities of agricultural enterprises based on the input parameters of human capital assessment. The developed model increases the manageability of agricultural business and contributes to the strengthening of the food supply system. The scientific novelty of the work is combined with the parameterization of human capital with the econometric analysis of production and food indicators, which makes it possible to move from descriptive estimates to quantitatively based management.

detail.abstract: Shariah-compliant stock screening has historically relied entirely on manual analysis by Shariah Supervisory Boards (SSBs). This paper presents a reproducible machine learning framework that treats AAOIFI Standard 21 (2017) compliance as a supervised classification problem, with the SSB verdicts as ground truth labels. detail.abstract:
This article declares and defines AI-Based Jurimetrics-a field that treats the disciplined collaboration between a human legal reasoner and artificial intelligence as both its object of study and its distinct practice. Rooted in the jurimetric tradition, the field differs in one fundamental respect: it does not treat artificial intelligence merely as a tool, but formulates the standards that render human-machine collaboration methodologically and ethically accountable. Four principles form its foundation: the non-negotiable verification of every cited norm against its primary source; sole substantive authority residing in the human, with artificial intelligence as instrument and not co-author; the open inventory of techniques born from the collaboration so that they may be tested and adopted; and disciplined continuity through a mechanism that makes those commitments keepable across time. The article sets out the field's framework of identity, its conceptual axes, and its operational principles, then affirms that the field is general across AI architectures and independent of any single model or vendor. As a marker, it invites other researchers to test, criticize, and develop it.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the impact of corporate digital transformation on environmental performance and the underlying mechanisms. Utilizing textual analysis of annual reports, we develop a fourdimensional measure of digital transformation comprising technological, business, manufacturing, and operational aspects. Analyzing data from Chinese A-share listed firms between 2009 and 2022, we demonstrate that corporate digital transformation significantly enhances environmental performance. While all dimensions of digital transformation contribute positively, manufacturing digital transformation exhibits the most substantial impact, followed by operational and technological digital transformation. We identify that green innovation, strengthened environmental monitoring and communication, increased environmental information transparency, and greater external attention are pivotal mechanisms through which digital transformation affects environmental performance, with transparency emerging as the strongest factor in this context. This paper offers new insights into the role of digital transformation in advancing sustainability.

detail.abstract: This paper examines how intergenerational inequality is expressed at labour-market entry by linking pre-adult economic hardship to early-career trajectories of labour-market risk and precarious employment. Using longitudinal data from the HILDA Survey, we model hardship dynamically over ages 4-24 and relate pre-adult trajectories to labour-market risk and precarious-employment pathways over ages 25-30. The results reveal substantial heterogeneity in both family disadvantage and early-adult labour-market experiences, showing that static measures of family background and adult outcomes miss important dimensions of inequality. Persistent hardship is strongly associated with persistently adverse early-career trajectories, while moving out of hardship, volatile hardship, and no hardship are linked to substantially lower probabilities of sustained disadvantage. Family resources partially moderate these associations, but the effects vary by resource type. Short-term insurance provides the clearest buffering role, reducing the likelihood of persistent and worsening disadvantage. Overall, the findings suggest that unequal family resources shape unequal capacity to absorb labour-market risk at the transition to adulthood, with family buffers operating primarily as private insurance against sustained disadvantage rather than as a mechanism supporting strategic tolerance of precarious work.

detail.abstract: We develop a Heterogeneous-Quantile Global VAR (HQGVAR) that allows each country-variable pair to enter the global system at its own quantile level. We provide a global admissibility result showing that we can assemble row-specific quantile equations into a stable reduced-form system with a valid moving-average representation and generalized impulse responses. The framework preserves the main structure of the GVAR but extends it to distributionally heterogeneous macro-financial environments. We establish large-sample theory for estimation and inference, justify moving-block bootstrap procedures, and show that the common-quantile QGVAR is a nested special case. Monte Carlo evidence demonstrates that heterogeneous-quantile modeling is valuable in the presence of heavy-tailed shocks, state-dependent spillovers, and asynchronous country-specific stress. In an application to a 13-economy macro-financial system, we do not reject system-wide equality with the median benchmark, but we detect localized, benchmark-referenced differences in financially and monetarily relevant transmission channels. Additional convergence, robustness, and forecast-validation diagnostics support the empirical implementation.

detail.abstract: This paper introduces indexification-a term that describes the structural transformation of equity markets caused by three decades of growth in price-insensitive passive investing. Drawing on the framework of complex adaptive systems (Brennan), the inelastic markets hypothesis (Gabaix and Koijen, 2021), and empirical evidence from momentum factor data, we argue that indexification has rewired the feedback architecture of markets in ways that systematically penalized strategies that previously generated alpha: value investing, mean reversion, high Active Share, and genuine diversification. If diversification is the only free lunch in investing, the free lunch counter closed around 2009. Markowitz's mathematically proven diversification benefit became expensive in practice when the structural bid flowed relentlessly into the index and only the index-though the counter may someday open under new management. The 2022 simultaneous collapse of stocks and bonds-worst since 1937-was a regime signal, not an anomaly. Two canaries in the coal mine-the post-2009 sign flip in Active Share and the deterioration of selling skill as measured by S4 (the Selling Skill Score, a framework measuring whether active managers' exit decisions add or destroy value relative to a hold)-provide observable evidence that indexification has been reshaping return dynamics since approximately 2009. We discuss the conditions under which indexification may short circuit, and what portfolio insulation-genuine asset class diversification-looks like when it does.

title: Evaluating AI Investment Strategies

detail.title: Evaluating AI Investment Strategies
detail.abstract: We study the problem of auditing a black-box algorithmic decision-maker from observable inputs and outputs alone. Our main result is an exact decomposition: under precisely characterized conditions, the cumulative regret of a dynamic policy equals the sum of per-period covariances between the cost vector and the policy's decision. This extends the single-period identity of Aldridge (2026) to the full multi-period setting of stochastic dynamic programming. We prove the identity holds exactly under i.i.d. costs and mean-unbiased Markov policies, derive closed-form bias corrections for non-stationary and time-varying cases, and establish the discounted-horizon analog. A Bellman recursion for the covariance regret functional connects the result to standard reinforcement learning algorithms; for rolling-window policies, the estimation-error bias is O(d/w). The decomposition has direct implications for algorithmic auditing in strategic environments: in platform mechanism design, it provides a welfare-based audit metric without access to the agent's private type; in repeated games, covariance reduction is a sufficient condition for policy improvement; in procurement and ad auctions, the bias correction quantifies welfare loss from strategic misreporting. The associated trajectory estimator is consistent, asymptotically normal with HAC variance, and computable in O(T • nd) time. This makes the proposed approach a tractable, model-free audit tool for platform mechanisms, algorithmic portfolio strategies, and any sequential decision system subject to external performance review.

detail.abstract:
We prove that for any signal derived from single-asset price features, the stan-
dard alpha metric—correlation with future returns—measures geometric cancella-
tion rather than predictive signal strength. We establish four results: (1) OLS-
estimated response gradients are structurally orthogonal to market movement di-
rections, with α⊥/α = 21.5× across 48 assets (p < 10−10); (2) traditional alpha falls
below 0.06 on average (p < 10−22); (3) position-return correlation exceeds signal-
return correlation by 7× (p < 10−12); and (4) the interaction kernel K = κf α ad-
mits an exact midpoint conservation law (Big Mac Theorem), verified to machine
epsilon. These results hold across equity, fixed income, commodity, and alternative
asset classes without per-asset tuning. In bear markets, the control-based strategy
achieves Sharpe +0.56 versus +0.35 for buy-and-hold (p = 0.013). We argue that
“alpha” in the traditional sense is a misdefined quantity, and propose that cur-
vature management—not direction prediction—is the correct framework for active
strategy evaluation.

detail.abstract: This paper develops a stochastic multi-sector climate-economy model to study how temperature targets, endogenous carbon pricing, and long-run macroeconomic risk shape sectoral asset prices. The model combines a reduced-form integrated assessment block with Epstein-Zin asset pricing. Sectors differ in productivity, carbon intensity, abatement costs, pass-through, and exposure to physical damages. For each temperature target, the policymaker commits to a target-consistent emissions path, and the carbon tax is determined endogenously, date by date and state by state, to implement it. The analysis delivers three main insights. First, stringent temperature targets are dominated by transition costs, whereas looser targets imply weaker transition pressure but larger long-run physical damages. Second, carbon intensity alone does not determine expected returns: endogenous carbon pricing can make brown sectors partly hedge-like, while stringent targets can generate substantial downside risk for high emitters. Third, once transition-cost and damage-exposure shifters are stochastic, the model generates both low-and highpremium brown-sector outcomes. The sign of the brown premium depends on the cyclicality of transition costs, pass-through, and the stochastic discount factor. The framework therefore connects climate targets to the cross section of sectoral risk premia in a tractable, scenario-consistent way.

detail.abstract: Global security conditions have become more uncertain than ever in recent years. In particular, the energy sector is experiencing rapid structural changes and a swift geopolitical realignment, while multiple factors—including the intensification of strategic competition between the United States and China, the prolonged Russia–Ukraine war, accelerated climate-change responses and energy transitions, and the launch of the second Trump administration in the United States—are intertwining to further deepen the instability of the international political order and the global energy market. Amid such a rapidly changing international environment, energy security is emerging as a core issue that combines national security, diplomatic strategy, and energy geopolitics. Against this backdrop, this study focuses on the strengthening cooperation between the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC), regarded as a key region for global energy supply, and China, the world’s largest energy importer. China is actively promoting the development of its renewable energy industry and related technologies to mitigate its high dependence on external energy sources and to accelerate the transition toward a low-carbon society. The GCC, leveraging its immense fossil-fuel supply capacity, is simultaneously pursuing industrial diversification and energy transition, and in doing so is expanding its demand for external cooperation in the field of environmentally friendly energy. Accordingly, the two sides are forming a mutually complementary cooperative relationship in the areas of fossil energy and clean energy, rapidly deepening the scope and level of their cooperation. (The rest omitted.)

detail.title: Distinguishing Drought Experiences: From Perception to Measurement and their Significance on Productivity Value in Uganda

publicationDetails.journalName: FEEM Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: Weather shocks increasingly threaten agricultural productivity in Sub-Saharan Africa. While the negative effects of drought on production have been documented in numerous studies, the behavioral dimension of adaptation, particularly how households perceive drought and what shapes these perceptions, remains less explored. The study focuses on Uganda to distinguish between selfreported drought (subjective) and data-driven drought (objective) and how their divergence is associated with agricultural outcomes. The study relies on four waves of household surveys (UNPS for 2009/10, 2010/11, 2011/12, and 2013/14) with historical re-analysis data on temperature and precipitation from 1981 to 2015. Log-linear and logit models are applied to estimate the association between drought, perception, and household characteristics on production and drought perception formation. Objective drought is negatively associated with total value of production. Subjective drought perception has a positive association with production. Self-reported drought captures differences in households' behavioral responses or preparedness, rather than observed weather shocks. Households that underestimate drought conditions tend to exhibit lower production outcomes, while households reporting a drought when this is not observed in objective data tend to maintain their production levels. Access to the Drought Early Warning System (DEWS), technology adoption, higher education levels, farming experience, and greater off-farm assets are positively associated with higher production. Conversely, lower production is associated with a higher share of female labor, female-headed households, and poverty. The results highlight the importance of distinguishing between perceived and observed drought and improving households' access to timely information to plan adaptation strategies.

title: Game Theory in Business and Trade Wars: A Comprehensive Analysis of Recent US Trade Policy Developments
affiliations: University of Delhi

detail.title: Game Theory in Business and Trade Wars: A Comprehensive Analysis of Recent US Trade Policy Developments
detail.abstract:
Background: The global trade environment between 2024 and 2025 has been characterised by renewed tariff escalation and unilateral policy actions led by the United States, significantly affecting international business strategy and global supply chains. The US Average Effective Tariff Rate (AETR) surged from 2.2% to 22.5% in 2025, a level unseen since the Smoot-Hawley Act of 1930. 
Methods: A mixed-methods approach is employed, combining quantitative data analysis with qualitative game-theoretic modelling. Trade policy is modelled as a non-cooperative, repeated game with three players (United States, China, India) whose payoffs are measured in GDP growth, Terms of Trade, and political capital. Data are drawn from the IMF World Economic Outlook (October 2025), the US International Trade Commission, Global Trade Alert, and the US Census Bureau. Results: Retaliatory tariffs, policy uncertainty, and weakened multilateral institutions increased operational risk, disrupted supply networks, and constrained firm-level strategic decision-making. US consumers bore approximately 90% of the tariff incidence. The IMF downgraded 2026 global growth forecasts to 2.7% (from 3.1%), and business investment contracted by 0.3% in Q1 2025. The US-China relationship exhibits a classic Prisoner's Dilemma structure (equilibrium payoff 3,3 vs. cooperative optimum 5,5), while the US-India relationship reflects asymmetric strategic interaction. 
Conclusions: Trade wars represent managerial and policy-level coordination failures in which rational actors settle into suboptimal but stable Nash equilibria. Key recommendations include coalition-based trade pressure, graduated reciprocity strategies, and "China Plus Two" supply chain diversification.

title: Regulating Environmental Weaponisation in the Digital Age
affiliations: University of College London, Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI) and University of Oxford - Oxford Internet Institute

detail.title: Regulating Environmental Weaponisation in the Digital Age
detail.abstract: In this article we examine digitally-enabled environmental weaponisation (EWD), the use of digital means to turn an environmental system into a medium of harm, so that the environment itself carries the harm beyond the point of attack. The harm has a distinctive structure. It begins as a digital operation and ends as a physical effect in the environment. The conversion between them occurs at a point of the infrastructure we name the point of transduction. Each of the established normative frameworks addresses one aspect of this harm, stopping at the boundary the harm crosses. As a result, EWD falls into the gap between them. Our thesis is that the assessment of EWD belongs at the point of transduction, and we offer two proposals that locate it there. The first governs the conduct of an attack. It presumes impermissible any operation whose foreseeable environmental harm the attacker cannot bound, and the burden of proof rests on them. The second governs the repair of the harm. It attaches the duty to repair to the harm itself, resting that duty on the responsible state and, where attribution fails, on the international community. Without these proposals the harm comes to rest, by default, on those EWD targets.

title: Lithium-ion battery health prediction using physical information and combined Bayesian ridge and Gaussian process regression
affiliations: Tsinghua University, Qingdao University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Dalian Jiaotong University, Weifang University and Qingdao University

detail.title: Lithium-ion battery health prediction using physical information and combined Bayesian ridge and Gaussian process regression
detail.abstract: To address the pronounced nonstationarity, weak cross-domain generalization, and strong dependence on target-domain labels in state-of-health (SOH) prediction for lithium-ion batteries under complex operating conditions, this paper proposes a zero-shot SOH prediction method that integrates physical information with high-frequency-sensitive modeling. First, an observer for latent physical states, including internal battery polarization, is constructed based on adaptive-noise extended Kalman filtering (AN-EKF), thereby extracting physically meaningful deep features from externally measured signals. Second, key health indicators are selected using the Pearson correlation coefficient, and a robust scaling mechanism based on the interquartile range (IQR) is incorporated to improve feature stability in cross-battery scenarios. On this basis, a dual-track modeling framework with trend-residual decoupling is designed. Bayesian ridge regression (BR) is used to characterize the global degradation trend, while Gaussian process regression (GPR) with a Matérn kernel is introduced to model high-frequency capacity-regeneration residuals, enabling refined fitting of complex nonlinear degradation trajectories. Meanwhile, an exponential-decay-based initial-state calibration strategy and an exponential moving average post-processing mechanism are proposed to enhance the initial stability and engineering deploy ability of the model under zero-shot conditions. Finally, zero-shot leave-one-battery-out cross-battery validation experiments are conducted on the NASA lithium-ion battery aging dataset. The results show that the proposed method significantly outperforms conventional models in prediction accuracy, robustness, and uncertainty quantification, and can achieve high-accuracy SOH prediction without target-domain labels, thereby providing an engineering-practical solution for safe battery management system operation and life assessment.

title: Distributive Justice and Liberty ～ Overlapping Conclusions from Utilitarianism and Deontology

detail.title: Distributive Justice and Liberty ～ Overlapping Conclusions from Utilitarianism and Deontology
detail.abstract: If we focus on mechanism of action choice, we can easily understand that combination of "principle of distributive justice" and "principle of liberty" can maximize the total sum of happiness. This means that justice is a general way to maximize utility; utilitarians and deontologists are not enemies in most cases. Thus, we are unanimous for these two general principles, which can tell us what to do in various areas (including normative ethics/economics and political/legal philosophy) much more precisely than before.

title: Isolating climate and financial risk in inland green hydrogen: A dependency-aware stochastic techno-economic analysis
affiliations: University of New South Wales (UNSW), University of New South Wales, University of New South Wales (UNSW) - School of Mechanical and Manufacturing Engineering and University of New South Wales (UNSW) - School of Chemical Engineering

detail.title: Isolating climate and financial risk in inland green hydrogen: A dependency-aware stochastic techno-economic analysis
detail.abstract: Inland green hydrogen production faces uncertainties that coastal techno-economic models often overlook. Existing probabilistic studies also tend to compare projects across countries, where climate effects are confounded by differences in financial conditions, regulation and sovereign risk. This study develops a dependency-aware stochastic techno-economic framework for a controlled within-jurisdiction comparison across three Köppen climate zones in Australia’s Murray–Darling Basin (MDB), to isolate climate zone effects independent of financial conditions, federal regulation and sovereign risk. Empirical climate resampling, copula-based macroeconomic sampling and stochastic feedwater conditions are propagated through an integrated photovoltaic–water treatment–electrolysis model. The model covers alkaline (AE) and proton-exchange-membrane (PEM) electrolyzers coupled with brackish-water reverse osmosis (RO) or low-temperature multi-effect distillation (LT-MED) and zero-liquid discharge (ZLD). Levelized cost of hydrogen (LCOH), the cost impact of water (CIoW) and 95% Value-at-Risk (VaR) are evaluated under climate-isolated, finance-isolated, combined-uncertainties and policy-adjusted scenarios. Results show that climatic uncertainty mainly shifts median LCOH, whereas financial uncertainty controls distribution width and tail risk. Stochastic median LCOH exceeds deterministic baselines by 34–39%. PEM pathways have larger VaR–LCOH gaps (1.25–1.43 USD kg⁻¹) than AE pathways (0.92–1.07 USD kg⁻¹), indicating that similar median costs can mask different downside exposures. Production subsidies reduce mean LCOH by 7.9-8.9% but leave the median and upper-tail risk unchanged. A single-site deterministic Coupled Model Intercomparison Project Phase 6 (CMIP6) stress test shows that a warming climate has only marginal thermal effects on LCOH. Cost reduction and risk reduction are therefore non-equivalent objectives, requiring dependency-aware and region-adaptive policy design.

title: Confidence-Aware Autonomous Cyber–Physical Security Control Framework for Therapeutic Internet of Medical Things Systems
affiliations: , affiliation not provided to SSRN and Kampala International University in Tanzania (KIUT)

detail.title: Confidence-Aware Autonomous Cyber–Physical Security Control Framework for Therapeutic Internet of Medical Things Systems
detail.abstract: The rapid expansion of therapeutic Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) devices within Cloud–IoT healthcare infrastructures introduces cyber–physical risks that extend beyond conventional network intrusion concerns. In therapeutic systems, security failures may directly impact physiological actuation and patient safety. Existing intrusion detection systems primarily optimize classification performance and rarely incorporate predictive uncertainty, clinical consequence, or availability constraints into mitigation logic. This paper proposes a confidence-aware autonomous security control framework that protects therapeutic actuation pathways rather than merely filtering malicious traffic. The architecture integrates a Deep Feedforward Neural Network (DFFNN) for intrusion detection, Monte Carlo Dropout for predictive uncertainty estimation, a severity-weighted cyber–physical risk model reflecting clinical harm potential, a multi-tier authorization policy (Allow–Degrade–Block), and constrained reinforcement learning formulated as a Constrained Markov Decision Process (CMDP) to enforce safety-aware adaptive optimization. Evaluated on the CICIoMT2024 dataset (872,034 training and 465,297 testing samples), the detection model achieved a ROC–AUC of 0.9991 with strong calibration (ECE = 0.00547). Under simulated threat escalation, static thresholding achieved 99.6% attack blocking but reduced benign continuity to 0.90, thereby increasing the risk of unintended therapy interruption. In contrast, the CMDP-based policy preserved near-perfect continuity (~1.0) while maintaining balanced attack prevention performance (0.53) under strict continuity constraints thereby demonstrating that effective therapeutic cybersecurity requires optimizing cyber-risk management without compromising uninterrupted and safe therapy delivery. These findings demonstrate that therapeutic cybersecurity must be reformulated as a regulated cyber–physical control system, enabling autonomous, safety-aware protection of clinical actuation in Cloud–IoT healthcare environments.

title: Anatomy of a Dissolving Anomaly: A Look-Ahead-Clean Audit of Payoff Asymmetry and an Overfitting-Resistant Framework for Validating Distributional Equity Signals
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Anatomy of a Dissolving Anomaly: A Look-Ahead-Clean Audit of Payoff Asymmetry and an Overfitting-Resistant Framework for Validating Distributional Equity Signals

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Noneq
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract: Distributional metrics of equity returns — skewness, tail indices, gain/loss ratios — are unusually easy to fool oneself with, because the same fat tails that make them interesting also break the standard estimators used to evaluate them. We take payoff asymmetry (PA), the ratio of mean conditional gains to mean conditional losses, as a representative case, and trace a single signal from a striking but spurious naive result down to a modest, honest residue. We make three contributions. First, empirical: computed prospectively over 106,163 stock-month observations (715 U.S. equities, 2009–2025), PA is a regime-independent inverse predictor of the typical (median) forward return, but the effect is not a tradeable mean premium and, in a six-factor horserace, survives only as a volatility-conditional refinement of the known lottery anomaly — within the most volatile quintile, low-PA names beat high-PA names by ~5% per month in median return (Newey-West t ≈ 3.8), with no effect among low-volatility names. Second, methodological: we document five distinct ways the naive analysis misleads — look-ahead contamination, the divergence of mean-based and rank-based inference under fat tails, overlapping- window dependence, circular ex-post conditioning, and a spurious overlapping momentum control — and show that each inflates or inverts the apparent result. Third, infrastructural: we develop a gating framework that subjects any candidate signal to look-ahead clean construction, distribution-free and autocorrelation-robust inference, a factor horserace, purged out-of-sample validation, and explicit multiple-testing penalties (the Deflated Sharpe Ratio and the Probability of Backtest Overfitting), together with a continuous-evaluation loop that tracks each candidate's robustness decay as new data arrives. The framework correctly ranks the surviving conditional effect, flags it as a median characteristic rather than a Sharpe-tradeable strategy, and reports a low probability of backtest overfitting (0.05) over its first search. The broader message is that under fat tails the choice of statistical methodology routinely determines not only the magnitude but the sign of a measured relationship, and that honest discovery requires the methodology to be adversarial to the researcher.

detail.abstract: We conduct a randomized online experiment with approximately 2,000 Mexican adults on the role of health-related information and front-of-package sugar warning labels. We find that supplementary health information, designed to challenge prior beliefs and prompt reflection, leads respondents to switch to products without high-sugar warnings, increases concern about public health, and builds support for policies limiting the consumption of sugary products. Warning labels alone have virtually no effect. However, responsive individuals tend to be highly educated, report good health, exercise regularly, and trust in science. These findings suggest that health information may fail to reduce unhealthy consumption among those most in need of intervention.

title: Information Ambiguity and Oil Volatility: Evidence from the U.S.-Iran Conflict
affiliations: Ningbo University of Finance and Economics and Ningbo University of Finance and Economics

detail.title: Information Ambiguity and Oil Volatility: Evidence from the U.S.-Iran Conflict
detail.abstract: We introduce non-severe event volatility (NSEV) as a measure of information ambiguity in the U.S.-Iran conflict. NSEV is the rolling 10-day standard deviation of daily non-severe regional event counts from GDELT, covering 2.4 million events from 2020 to 2026. In the 90-day window preceding the February 28, 2026 escalation, NSEV exhibits strong co-movement with the CBOE Crude Oil Volatility Index (OVX), explaining 66.7% of its variation and rising to 79.0% with controls. Across four episodes, NSEV shows strong pre-crisis correlation only for the 2026 escalation involving direct U.S. action (0.817), with weaker correlations for the Soleimani killing (0.750) and Iran-Israel tensions (0.583), and none for the COVID-19 pandemic (-0.181). Severe kinetic events contribute limited incremental power. OVX is associated with the volatility of non-kinetic information flows rather than kinetic events themselves.

title: Money as Final Settlement Authority: An Institutional Theory of Monetary Closure

detail.title: Money as Final Settlement Authority: An Institutional Theory of Monetary Closure
detail.abstract: This paper develops an institutional theory of money as final settlement authority. It argues that money is not primarily a commodity, physical object, mere credit relation, or functional medium of exchange, but an institutional instrument that carries institutionally authorized and socially recognized settlement authority to discharge debts and obligations finally. The paper identifies settlement uncertainty as the institutional friction that money addresses. In societies structured by debts and obligations, agents require mechanisms through which obligations can be closed without residual enforceable claims. Monetary instruments reduce this uncertainty by linking authorization, recognition, acceptance, discharge, and finality. In doing so, the paper identifies money as a specific kind of institution: an institution for closing obligations. It reconstructs the standard functions of money as derivative expressions of monetary closure and distinguishes 2 of 23 credit from money: credit opens, extends, or transfers obligations, while money closes them. The paper offers a foundational account of monetary closure and a framework for analyzing variation in moneyness across institutional domains.

title: Thickness as Collateral: Demand Aggregation, Asset Utilization, and Endogenous Credit Inclusion

detail.title: Thickness as Collateral: Demand Aggregation, Asset Utilization, and Endogenous Credit Inclusion
detail.abstract: In developing economies, smallholder farmers who could profitably mechanize cannot finance an indivisible asset-a tractor-lacking collateral where resale markets are thin. We model a digital platform that aggregates dispersed demand, raising each machine's utilization and creating a relational rent-the platform premium-that an operator forfeits if excluded for default. Exclusion substitutes for collateral, making unsecured credit self-enforcing; because the premium grows with matching-market thickness, enforcement is endogenous to network density. We characterize an inclusion threshold, an enforcement poverty trap escapable by a big push, progressive but distorted credit access, and a self-limiting platform monopoly.

title: SPANDAN -Smart Preventive And Non-invasive Diagnostic Access Network

detail.title: SPANDAN -Smart Preventive And Non-invasive Diagnostic Access Network

declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. The work was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract: Globally, healthcare systems remain predominantly reactive — engineered to treat illness rather than prevent it. In Bangladesh, this limitation is critically compounded by infrastructural deficits: approximately 50.4 million rural citizens lack consistent access to primary diagnostic services [WHO, 2023], healthcare worker density falls below the WHO minimum threshold [World Bank, 2022], and non-communicable diseases, including hypertension, diabetes, and cardiovascular conditions, are rising at alarming rates [Bangladesh Health Bulletin, 2022]. Existing technological interventions — commercial wearables, IoT monitoring platforms, and standalone AI diagnostic tools — remain fragmented, urban-centric, power-grid-dependent, and incapable of delivering integrated preventive intelligence in resource-constrained environments [Malasinghe et al., 2019; Guk et al., 2019]. This paper presents SPANDAN (Smart Preventive And Non-invasive Diagnostic Access Network), a solar-powered, offline-capable, AI-assisted community health kiosk engineered for underserved populations in Bangladesh. SPANDAN integrates a seven-parameter non-invasive multimodal sensor array — blood pressure, SpO₂, heart rate variability, body temperature, body weight, three-lead ECG, and near-infrared indicative glucose screening — within a low-cost ARM-based embedded platform. Patient identity is managed through NID-based verification with SHA-256 hashing and AES-256-GCM encryption, ensuring privacy-preserving longitudinal records without cloud dependency during offline operation. Clinical decisions are delivered through a dual-layer Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS): an offline rule-based engine calibrated against established WHO, AHA, and IDF clinical guidelines with region-specific parameters for Bangladesh’s diverse epidemiological contexts; and an AI-assisted reasoning layer that provides contextual triage support when connectivity is available. All assessments follow a four-tier risk classification framework (GREEN/YELLOW/ORANGE/RED), enabling early warning, preventive intervention, and remote healthcare escalation through integrated telemedicine services. This paper presents the complete V1 system architecture, hardware specification, software stack, security framework, and deployment economic model of SPANDAN — not merely as a diagnostic device, but as a paradigm shift from episodic, facility-bound healthcare toward continuous, community-embedded, intelligent health protection for those who need it most.

title: What The Missing Middle Is Actually Missing: The Mortgage Market Why Ontario's "Missing Middle" Housing Studies Misdiagnose The Affordability Crisisand What The Evidence Says Is Actually Driving Prices

detail.title: What The Missing Middle Is Actually Missing: The Mortgage Market Why Ontario's "Missing Middle" Housing Studies Misdiagnose The Affordability Crisisand What The Evidence Says Is Actually Driving Prices

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflicts to declare
declarations.funderStatement: Self-funded

detail.abstract: Canada's most influential housing-shortage analyses-the Missing Middle Initiative and allied reports - model the affordability crisis as a quantity problem: the supply of dwellings against a population-driven count of households. Across nine such reports no model of price appears, and the terms monetary policy, money creation, and credit creation appear zero times. This study argues that the omission is decisive. House prices are set by the credit available to the marginal buyer: because a mortgage is sized by the amortization identity at a fixed monthly payment, a lower policy rate enlarges the loan a given income can carry, and the additional credit is capitalized into price. The largest movement in Canadian house prices in modern history-the 2020-2022 run-up and the correction that followed-tracked the Bank of Canada's policy rate almost to the month, while supply changed only slowly. Reverse-engineering the 2022-2023 regional corrections shows that attributing them to supply would have required building eight to eleven times the homes actually completed, whereas the rate move alone more than accounts for the decline. The paper grounds the mechanism in the central banks' own description of money creation through commercial-bank lending (Bank of England 2014, with corroborating statements from the Bundesbank, the European Central Bank, the Bank of Canada and others), and develops the distributional incidence of monetary policy and the financialization of rental housing. It concludes that supply-side measures, while warranted on other grounds, cannot lower the price level while credit is the binding constraint; the effective levers are credit conditions and non-market housing.

title: Pareto's Counterfeit Efficiency and the Fallacy of a Universe without Uncertainty How the Welfare Theorems, the Efficient-Markets Hypothesis, and the Marginal Cost of Funds Rest on a Single Premise

detail.title: Pareto's Counterfeit Efficiency and the Fallacy of a Universe without Uncertainty How the Welfare Theorems, the Efficient-Markets Hypothesis, and the Marginal Cost of Funds Rest on a Single Premise

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflicts
declarations.funderStatement: Self-funded

detail.abstract:
The word “efficient” carries, in economic argument, an authority borrowed from engineering, where it names a cardinal ratio of useful output to input with a hard physical ceiling and a definite maximand. This paper argues that the efficiency invoked to remove policies from consideration such as a minimum wage that is “inefficient,” a tax that imposes a “deadweight loss,” or a public programme that carries an excessive “marginal cost of funds” all rely on borrowed credibility from the engineering definition, with which it has nothing in common. Allocative, or Pareto, efficiency is a definition rather than a finding: true by construction, silent on distribution, and functioning as a one-way rule that ratifies whatever distribution it begins from. Its rhetorical force is inherited by the first fundamental theorem of welfare economics and, through it, by the efficient-markets hypothesis and the marginal cost of funds.

The paper’s principal claim is that this family of results rests on a single premise: the absence of irreducible uncertainty. That premise is not confined to two assumptions but recurs across a family of total-information constructions — the efficient-markets hypothesis, complete contingent markets, rational expectations, and the monetarist treatment of money as an already-created object — each of which, restated in information-theoretic terms, asserts that no residual uncertainty exists. The premise is refuted in three ways: by ordinary institutions whose entire function is the management of unresolved uncertainty (insurance, hedging, interest, and the wider Finance–Insurance–Real-Estate sector); by the orthodoxy’s own demonstration that incomplete markets are generically constrained inefficient; and by economic crises themselves, which are the breaking of financial bonds that a fully-priced future could not produce. Once the premise is set aside, the doctrine’s central verdict inverts: the work of reducing uncertainty — redundancy, reserves, regulation, insurance, maintenance, public investment — ceases to be deadweight and is seen as the means by which an open economic system builds order against decay.

title: How Assumptions Without Content Collapse the Models they Define Interpretation, Stakes, and the Standard of Due Diligence in Economic Method

detail.title: How Assumptions Without Content Collapse the Models they Define Interpretation, Stakes, and the Standard of Due Diligence in Economic Method

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No conflicts.
declarations.funderStatement: Self-funded

detail.abstract:
Economics presents itself as a science while, in an influential family of results, behaving like the least disciplined kind of interpretation. This paper develops a methodological principle to make the contrast precise: the degree of interpretive multiplicity a domain may legitimately tolerate is inversely proportional to the stakes of being wrong and to the strength of the feedback loop available to test a reading against the world. In the interpretation of make-believe — literature, where being wrong is play — several readings of one signal may coexist, and this is disciplined density rather than vagueness. As stakes rise and a feedback loop becomes available, readings must be narrowed by two checks: internal interrogation of the interpretive theory for unjustified premises, and external comparison against real-world data.

The paper argues that a class of economic assumptions — the family of total-information premises underlying the efficient-markets hypothesis, complete contingent markets, rational expectations, and the quantity-theoretic treatment of money — fails both checks. Stated in information-theoretic terms, each asserts the absence of residual uncertainty: a premise true by construction and contradicted by ordinary evidence, yet exempted from revision. Distinguishing such a contentless premise from legitimate idealisation turns on a single test, whether the assumption can be perturbed without collapsing the result. Because economic conclusions are consequential in the manner that makes professions of medicine, engineering, and law, the paper concludes that assumptions of this kind are owed a standard of due diligence the discipline does not at present impose, and sketches what that standard would require. The argument is offered not against formalism but in favour of more of it, directed where it is presently withheld: at the premises.

detail.abstract: This article analyzes the relationship between economic growth and unemployment through a comparative study of Okun's law applied to Morocco, Brazil, and Spain. Using annual data from the World Bank's World Development Indicators over the period 1991-2024, the study examines the extent to which real GDP growth explains annual variations in the unemployment rate across different economic contexts. The methodology is based on ordinary least squares (OLS) estimation, complemented by ADF stationarity tests, HAC robust standard errors, and dynamic lagged models. The results show that the coefficient associated with real GDP growth is negative and statistically significant in all three countries, broadly confirming the empirical validity of Okun's law. However, the intensity of this relationship varies substantially : it appears weakest in Morocco, intermediate in Brazil, and strongest in Spain. These findings suggest that economic growth contributes to explaining unemployment fluctuations, but remains insufficient to fully account for the broader dynamics of the labor market.

detail.abstract: Since the 1990s, the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) has reported much more rapid growth in U.S. private sector employer establishments than has the Census Bureau – the gap reached roughly 1.6 million by 2023. Using linked BLS-Census microdata, we document two main drivers. title: Using Web Services to Retrieve Real-Time Alternative Routes for Passenger Transport

detail.title: Using Web Services to Retrieve Real-Time Alternative Routes for Passenger Transport
detail.abstract: This study investigates the design and implementation of a web service architecture for retrieving real-time alternative routes in passenger transport systems. The proliferation of connected vehicles, mobile sensing platforms, and intelligent transportation infrastructures has generated unprecedented volumes of spatial-temporal data, enabling dynamic route optimization beyond static navigation approaches. Traditional routing algorithms rely on historical traffic patterns and fixed network graphs, which fail to adapt to rapidly changing conditions such as accidents, congestion spikes, weather disruptions, or temporary road closures. By leveraging web services that aggregate live data streams from heterogeneous sources—including traffic sensors, GPS trajectories, public transit feeds, and crowd-sourced incident reports—this research demonstrates a scalable framework for computing and disseminating alternative route options with minimal latency. The proposed system employs a microservices architecture, where each service encapsulates a distinct function: data ingestion from diverse APIs, real-time traffic state estimation, multi-criteria route optimization, and user-specific notification delivery. A key innovation is the integration of a parallelized shortest-path algorithm that evaluates multiple objectives simultaneously—travel time, fuel consumption, road safety, and user preference—using a Pareto-optimal approach. The service layer abstracts the complexity of underlying data fusion and computational geometry, exposing lightweight RESTful endpoints that client applications can query on demand. Experimental evaluation using a simulated metropolitan network with over ten thousand nodes and real-time traffic injection shows that the web service can produce alternative routes within sub-second response times, even under high concurrency loads. Findings indicate that dynamic rerouting enabled by this web service reduces average trip duration by up to eighteen percent compared to static routing baselines, while also distributing traffic load more evenly across the network, thereby mitigating secondary congestion. The architecture supports both private vehicle users and public transport passengers by incorporating multimodal transfer points and schedule adherence metrics. Furthermore, the modular design allows seamless integration with emerging technologies such as unmanned aerial vehicles for last-mile delivery and connected autonomous vehicles, aligning with contemporary trends in mobility as a service. This research contributes a validated blueprint for real-time, web-based route advisory systems that are essential for smart city initiatives aiming to enhance urban mobility efficiency, reduce environmental impact, and improve passenger satisfaction in increasingly dynamic transport environments.

title: Assessment of Occupational Radiation Exposure from Natural Radioactivity in Quarries of Nyandarua County, Kenya
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Assessment of Occupational Radiation Exposure from Natural Radioactivity in Quarries of Nyandarua County, Kenya
detail.abstract: The radiological hazards associated with quarry soils from Nyandarua County, Kenya, were investigated to assess the natural radioactivity levels and evaluate occupational risks. Thirty-six subsoil samples from Captain, Malewa, and Kiambaga quarries were analysed for 226Ra, 232Th, and 40K using high-purity germanium gamma-ray spectrometry. Mean activity concentrations were 35.6 Bq/kg  (range: 18-52) for 226Ra, 81.5 Bq/kg (57-104) for 232Th, and 1024 Bq/kg (498-1390) for 40K, exceeding UNSCEAR global averages by factors of 1.1, 1.8, and 2.4, respectively. Calculated hazard indices yielded: radium equivalent activity (231 Bq/kg), external hazard index (0.62), absorbed dose rate (108 nGy/h), annual effective dose equivalent (0.13 mSv/y), annual gonadal equivalent dose (772 μSv/y), and excess lifetime cancer risk (0.46 ×10-3). While Raeq, Hex, D, and AEDE remained below their recommended safety limits, both AGED and ELCR exceeded global averages by 157% and 54%, respectively. The elevated 232Th, and 40K concentrations, attributed to the region’s volcanic geology, contribute significantly to gamma exposure. Although immediate radiological risk is low, the elevated AGED and ELCR values indicate potential long-term health concerns from prolonged occupational exposure. These findings establish crucial baseline data and underscore the  need for continuous monitoring and implementation of radiation safety protocols in quarry operations.

title: Before the Commitment: Pre-Approval Analytical Engagement and Investment Decision Quality in Project Governance

detail.title: Before the Commitment: Pre-Approval Analytical Engagement and Investment Decision Quality in Project Governance
detail.abstract: Organizations commit to projects before the analytical work needed to justify that commitment has been completed, producing poor investment selection rather than poor execution. This study examines pre-approval analytical engagement and Investment Decision Quality (IDQ) through a mixed-methods design combining a survey of 138 investment decision participants with case analysis of 15 organizations, drawing on 53 interviews and 132 documents. Pre-approval engagement was strongly associated with IDQ (β = 0.58, p < .001), with engagement form explaining 38% of IDQ variance above controls. Governance processes without structured pre-approval analysis produced poor investment decisions at more than five times the rate of independent processes (37% versus 7%). The Stage 1 to Stage 2 transition established a governance threshold rather than a linear dosage relationship (Δ = −0.8). Analytical independence explained significant incremental IDQ variance above engagement presence and form (β = 0.33, p = .003). This study introduces IDQ as an empirically measurable project governance construct distinct from execution quality and extends front-end loading theory upstream of project initiation.

detail.abstract: Companies today face not only competitive problems but systemic problems. Classical strategy frameworks that define markets as industries, organizations as machines and the future as a linear extension of the past are increasingly insufficient in dynamic, interdependent and complex environments. The Schließmann approach therefore broadens strategic management through three perspectives: the definition of the Strategically Relevant Market (SRM), the positioning of the firm in the Schließmann Strategy Cube and the assessment of viability in the relevant system. The third axis of the cube-systemic viability-must remain open and system-specific. Its parameters cannot be standardized ex ante; they must be identified, assessed and, where possible, measured in their interdependencies and contributions to complexity. This revised version clarifies the Viability Matrix as a complexity-sensitive diagnostic framework. It does not treat agility and robustness as isolated virtues, but reads them in relation to the complexity structure of the relevant system. The paper integrates the "Octopus Organization" metaphor with the Schließmann Strategy Cube and the Viability Matrix. It argues that the octopus concept can refine, but must not replace, the third axis. It serves as a qualitative lens for sensing, interpreting and developing organizational capabilities such as decentralized intelligence, customer proximity, learning loops, responsibility close to the problem and leadership as system architecture. The resulting synthesis offers companies a more robust way to understand their real strategic playing field, diagnose systemic viability risks and translate complexity analysis into organizational development.

title: Auction Competitive Capacity: Characterization and Inference

detail.title: Auction Competitive Capacity: Characterization and Inference
detail.abstract: We axiomatize a measure of competitive pressure in auctions. Within the class of separable evidence indices-a template that fixes multiplicative separability and the top-two bid ratio as the competitive signal-nine structural axioms of participation, competition, and dispersion pin the index up to an ordinally irrelevant unit and one substantive dispersion calibration, which a tenth axiom fixes. The calibrated representative is ACC = H(p) • log(1 + p/G *), where H(p) is the Shannon entropy of bid shares, p is the top-two bid ratio, and G * is the normalized Gini dispersion of bids. The index is scale-invariant, concave in the precision ratio P/G * , and its evidence factors multiply, so log-evidence adds across auctions. ACC requires no equilibrium assumptions; in second-price auctions with truthful bidding, holding participation and dispersion fixed, it is increasing in p, which in that setting is the revenue extraction ratio. The index measures revealed competitive capacity, not certified honest competition: a perfect-mimicry impossibility result delimits what bids alone can identify, and a finite-resolution estimand handles tied bids on discrete grids. We prove the top-two ratio behavior for benchmark distributions in each extreme value domain, exactly at every sample size for Uniform and Pareto, and state the affine scaling law E[ACC n ] = c log n + d F as a conjecture supported by Monte Carlo. We provide √ T-consistent estimation with bootstrap inference, apply the index to collusion screening in Operation Car Wash procurement data, and illustrate it on eBay auctions. Whether the composite index improves on its separate components remains the main open empirical question.

title: Emergence, the Flat Ontology Challenge, and the Flourishing Landscape Ontology
affiliations: NYU Stern School of Business

detail.title: Emergence, the Flat Ontology Challenge, and the Flourishing Landscape Ontology
detail.abstract: Brian Greene has argued that emergence -- the spontaneous self-organization of simpler things into more complex ones -- explains the remarkable order and vitality of the universe without requiring purpose or design. This paper accepts that argument fully and then argues it is incomplete. The question is not whether emergence is real, but whether it operates on a flat ontological landscape where any randomly emergent structure has an equal probability of persisting. A flat ontology should produce a world weighted toward maximum entropy, Boltzmann brains, and parasitic dominance. What we observe instead, across six genuinely independent empirical domains from molecular biology to ancient civilization, is a preponderance of systems exhibiting the specific architecture of feedback preservation, exploit suppression, and part-whole alignment -- the Listening Learning Correcting and Realigning with reality architecture. This preponderance is not predicted by flat ontology and cannot be explained by it without accumulating independent auxiliary hypotheses for each domain. The Flourishing Landscape Ontology (FLO) explains it with one principle: existence is curved. The ontological landscape favors the formation and persistence of flourishing systems without requiring it, the way rolling terrain favors lakes and streams without eliminating desolate peaks. The paper presents cross-domain empirical evidence, four lines of theoretical consilience (holonic evolutionary transitions, Noether's theorem as physical feedback preservation, Waddington's developmental canalization, and the Wolfram-Hopkins synthesis of regulated wildness), and the Regulated Wildness Law -- a formal proposal that the harmonic mean of Watching and Correction scores predicts durability better than their sum, pilot-confirmed across 48 cases (p=0.0006). Three candidate explanations for the curvature are considered. The theological landing point -- a world that bends toward shalom without requiring it, consistent with Psalm 23 -- is the most parsimonious available explanation.

title: The Business-Fluent Lawyer: Key Concepts in Technology, Governance, Ethics, and Behavioral Science for Legal Practice
